description: issue #953, the in-budget control twin of wait-over-budget-limit: `wait 3` under the SAME deliberately small instruction budget of 5 completes cleanly and emits its trailing `primitive` event, so that fixture's ol-limit is caused by the pause being longer than the budget and not merely by a budget too small for any program. Since #953 -- normative since #1034 (spec/interaction-events.md's `### wait <n>`: "Each tick a `wait` advances costs one instruction against the execution budget") -- a `wait` tick is itself one charged instruction, so the cost of `wait n` is n on top of the statement's own charge: `wait n` completes exactly when n < budget. 3 < 5 here; 8 is not < 5 in the twin. The pause completing is what emits the `primitive` (spec/interaction-events.md: "wait emits a `primitive` event after the pause completes"), so its presence here and absence there is the whole observable difference.
